name: SD at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: South Dakota's R+15 partisan lean in an open seat
Jackley's large fundraising and cash advantage over Gronli
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The seat's R+15 lean and the open-seat fundamentals point to a solid Republican hold, and Marty Jackley has out-raised Nikki Gronli by roughly five to one with a large cash-on-hand edge. Markets price a Republican win near 95%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Gronli within single digits, or a major Jackley scandal, would be the main signal to move this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dusty Johnson (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
South Dakota's at-large House seat is open after Dusty Johnson retired to run for governor, but the district's strong Republican lean remains the dominant fact of the race. Marty Jackley, the well-funded Republican, faces Democrat Nikki Gronli, who has raised only a fraction of his total and holds modest cash reserves. No independent groups have spent against Jackley, and no general-election polls are available.

With no expert ratings and thin polling, the forecast rests on the district's R+15 lean, the large financial gap, and prediction markets pricing a Republican win around 95%. A Republican hold is the clear expectation, with Gronli needing an unusual shift to compete.
